**Chapter Five: Chemical Bond**

We know, all substances consist of molecules and atoms. Each of these matters has its own atoms. Out of these substances, atoms of one or more elements make a substance's molecule. Atoms do not remain scattered in the molecule of substances. They remain highly organized. The force of attraction that binds two atoms in a molecule is called chemical bond. This bond may be of various kinds- ionic bond, covalent bond or metallic bond etc. This chapter will focus upon compounds made of ionic bonds, covalent bonds or metallic bonds, their process of bonding and their properties.

Description: A molecular model of a substance with atoms bonded together.

**5.1 Introduction to Chemical Bond**

Chemical bond is the force of attraction that binds two or more atoms in a molecule. There are three types of chemical bonds: ionic bond, covalent bond, and metallic bond.

**5.2 Ionic Bond**

Ionic bond is the force of attraction between two oppositely charged ions. It is formed when one or more electrons are transferred from one atom to another. The resulting ions have opposite charges, which attract each other.

[DIAGRAM]
Caption: Fig 5.2
Callouts: 
Description: A diagram showing the formation of an ionic bond between two atoms.

**5.3 Covalent Bond**

Covalent bond is the force of attraction between two or more atoms that share one or more pairs of electrons. It is formed when two or more atoms share one or more pairs of electrons to achieve a full outer energy level.

[DIAGRAM]
Caption: Fig 5.3
Callouts: 
Description: A diagram showing the formation of a covalent bond between two atoms.

**5.4 Metallic Bond**

Metallic bond is the force of attraction between the positive ions and the electrons in a metal. It is formed when the electrons in a metal are delocalized, meaning they are free to move throughout the metal.

[DIAGRAM]
Caption: Fig 5.4
Callouts: 
Description: A diagram showing the formation of a metallic bond in a metal.

**5.5 Conclusion**

In conclusion, chemical bond is the force of attraction that binds two or more atoms in a molecule. There are three types of chemical bonds: ionic bond, covalent bond, and metallic bond. Each type of bond has its own unique characteristics and properties. Understanding chemical bonds is important for understanding the properties and behavior of substances.
